speaker: Unknown
en: You built and led Facebook news feeds.
zh: 你建立并领导了 Facebook 动态消息。

speaker: Unknown
en: You shipped the Messenger app as its own app.
zh: 你将 Messenger 应用作为独立应用发布了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You launched ChatGPT Enterprise.
zh: 你推出了 ChatGPT Enterprise。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's an important lesson you've learned about what it takes to succeed building something from idea to one to billions?
zh: 关于从想法到数十亿用户的成功构建，你学到的一个重要教训是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to plan your chess moves out in advance.
zh: 你必须提前计划好你的国际象棋步骤。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to really think before you act and build systems that were going to let you go sustainably faster.
zh: 你必须在行动前真正思考，并建立能让你的速度持续更快的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the most counterintuitive lesson you've learned?
zh: 你学到的最反直觉的教训是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes your product actually doesn't matter.
zh: 有时你的产品实际上并不重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: At Uber, I learned this because, really, the price and the ETA at Uber was the product.
zh: 在 Uber，我学到了这一点，因为实际上，Uber 的价格和 ETA 就是产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Looking at it from a holistic perspective, we humans consume the entirety of the product.
zh: 从整体角度来看，我们人类消费的是产品的全部。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not to say that you shouldn't fix the bug, but it doesn't have as much of an impact as something that is more important to people.
zh: 这并不是说你不应该修复那个错误，但它的影响力不如那些对人们更重要的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's one specific thing you think will change in a big way with AI that people don't think enough about?
zh: 你认为 AI 会在哪一方面发生巨大改变，而人们对此思考得还不够？

speaker: Unknown
en: Education is going to change.
zh: 教育将会改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: My son, he was nine at the time, built a custom GPT that you can type in any topic and it would give you a sentence that had every letter of the English alphabet.
zh: 我的儿子，他当时九岁，构建了一个自定义 GPT，你可以输入任何话题，它会给你一个包含英语字母表中每个字母的句子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Isn't that mind-blowing?
zh: 这难道不令人惊叹吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I can already see his brain rewiring.
zh: 我已经可以看到他的大脑正在重新布线。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's one thing you look for in people you hire?
zh: 你在招聘的人身上寻找的一件事是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: In 6 months, if I'm telling you what to do, I've hired the wrong person.
zh: 在 6 个月内，如果我还要告诉你该做什么，我就招错了人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It helps me and the person operate on a different level where the goal is not, did you hit this OKR?
zh: 这有助于我和这个人在不同的层面上运作，在那个层面上，目标并不是「你是否达到了这个 OKR？」

speaker: Unknown
en: The Meta goal becomes, are we calibrating enough?
zh: Meta 目标变成了，我们的校准是否足够？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are we actually getting into a spot where in 6 months you're the one telling me what needs to be done?
zh: 我们实际上是否进入了一个状态，在 6 个月后是你来告诉我需要做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's something you've learned about what it takes to be a great product person?
zh: 关于成为优秀产品人需要具备什么，你学到了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there are five different types of product managers.
zh: 我认为有五种不同类型的产品经理。

speaker: Unknown
en: Number one is-
zh: 第一个是——

speaker: Unknown
en: Today my guest is Peter Deng.
zh: 今天我的嘉宾是 Peter Deng。

speaker: Unknown
en: Peter is maybe the most under the radar impactful Product Leader that you have never heard of.
zh: Peter 也许是你听说过的最低调、最具影响力的产品领导者。

speaker: Unknown
en: I often say that the best product people are not the people on Twitter and LinkedIn sharing advice, but the people who don't have time to do that because they're too busy doing the work.
zh: 我常说，最好的产品人不是在 Twitter 和 LinkedIn 上分享建议的人，而是那些因为忙于工作而没有时间这样做的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Peter is the epitome of this.
zh: Peter 就是这方面的典范。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was VP of product at OpenAI where he oversaw product design and engineering for ChatGPT and helped ship ChatGPT Enterprise, voice, memory, desktop, custom GPTs and more.
zh: 他是 OpenAI 的产品副总裁，负责监督 ChatGPT 的产品设计和工程，并协助发布了 ChatGPT Enterprise、语音、记忆、桌面版、自定义 GPT 等产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: He also oversaw and built their first growth team.
zh: 他还监督并建立了他们的第一个增长团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was the first Head of Product at Instagram where he worked closely with Mike and Kevin, and oversaw all product development, including on content sharing, ads, growth, even helped build out their design and user research functions.
zh: 他是 Instagram 的第一任产品负责人，与 Mike 和 Kevin 密切合作，监督了所有产品开发，包括内容分享、广告、增长，甚至协助建立了他们的设计和用户研究职能。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was also a Head of the Rider product team at Uber where he oversaw everything in the Rider app, including big improvements to pickups and drop-offs at Uber Pool and airports.
zh: 他也是 Uber Rider 产品团队的负责人，监督了 Rider 应用中的所有内容，包括对 Uber Pool 和机场接送的重大改进。

speaker: Unknown
en: He also helped the team launch new products including Uber Reserve, which is now approaching a $5 billion a year business.
zh: 他还协助团队发布了新产品，包括 Uber Reserve，该业务目前的年营收接近 50 亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: He also spent nearly 10 years at Facebook as their 4th ever Product Manager where he built and led the team behind the current Newsfeed product, the standalone Messenger app, also photos, and groups, and homepage, and profiles.
zh: 他还在 Facebook 工作了近 10 年，作为其第 4 位产品经理，建立并领导了当前动态消息产品、独立 Messenger 应用、以及照片、群组、主页和个人资料背后的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was also Chief Product Officer at Airtable where he helped the company systemize how they built products and transitioned to Enterprise.
zh: 他还是 Airtable 的首席产品官，协助公司系统化了他们构建产品的方式并转型为企业级服务。

speaker: Unknown
en: He also led product management at Oculus.
zh: 他还领导了 Oculus 的产品管理。

speaker: Unknown
en: These days he is General Partner at Felicis where he is able to bring everything he's learned to more founders as an investor.
zh: 如今他是 Felicis 的普通合伙人，作为一名投资者，他能够将他学到的一切带给更多的创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: He has never done a podcast before or shared any of these lessons or stories publicly.
zh: 他以前从未做过播客，也没有公开分享过这些教训和故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you are in for a real treat.
zh: 所以，你将有幸听到这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: A huge thank you to Eric Antonow, Nick Turley, Lauren Motomati, Joanne Jain, and Sundeep Jain for contributing questions and topics.
zh: 非常感谢 Eric Antonow、Nick Turley、Lauren Motomati、Joanne Jain 和 Sundeep Jain 贡献的问题和话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: This conversation, if you enjoy this podcast, don't forget to subscribe and follow it in your favorite podcasting app or YouTube.
zh: 这段对话，如果你喜欢这个播客，别忘了在你最喜欢的播客应用或 YouTube 中订阅和关注它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, if you become an annual subscriber of my newsletter, you get a year free of a bunch of amazing products including Bolt, Linear, Superhuman, Notion, Perplexity and Granola.
zh: 另外，如果你成为我简报的年度订阅者，你可以免费使用一年一系列很棒的产品，包括 Bolt、Linear、Superhuman、Notion、Perplexity 和 Granola。

speaker: Unknown
en: Check it out at lennysnewsletter.com and click bundle.
zh: 请访问 lennysnewsletter.com 并点击 bundle 查看。

speaker: Unknown
en: With that, I bring you Peter Deng.
zh: 有了这些，我为你带来 Peter Deng。

speaker: Unknown
en: Many of you are building AI products, which is why I am very excited to chat with Brandon Foo, founder and CEO of Paragon.
zh: 你们很多人都在构建 AI 产品，这就是为什么我非常兴奋能与 Paragon 的创始人兼 CEO Brandon Foo 聊天。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey Brandon.
zh: 嘿 Brandon。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey Lenny.
zh: 嘿 Lenny。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for having me.
zh: 谢谢邀请我。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, integrations have become a big deal for AI products.
zh: 所以，集成对 AI 产品来说已经变得非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why is that?
zh: 为什么会这样？

speaker: Unknown
en: Integrations are mission-critical for AI for two reasons: First, AI products need contacts from their customer's business data such as Google Drive files, Slack messages or CRM records.
zh: 集成对 AI 来说是关键任务，原因有二：首先，AI 产品需要来自其客户业务数据的联系人，例如 Google Drive 文件、Slack 消息或 CRM 记录。

speaker: Unknown
en: Second, for AI products to automate work on behalf of users, AI agents need to be able to take action across these different third-party tools.
zh: 其次，为了让 AI 产品代表用户自动化工作，AI 智能体需要能够跨这些不同的第三方工具采取行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, where does Paragon fit into all this?
zh: 那么，Paragon 在这一切中处于什么位置？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, these integrations are a pain to build, and that's why Paragon provides an embedded platform that enables engineers to ship these product integrations in just days instead of months across every use case from RAG data ingestion to a Agentic actions.
zh: 嗯，这些集成构建起来很痛苦，这就是为什么 Paragon 提供了一个嵌入式平台，使工程师能够在几天内而不是几个月内发布这些产品集成，涵盖从 RAG 数据摄取到智能体行动的每个用例。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I know from firsthand experience that maintenance is even harder than just building it for the first time.
zh: 而且我从第一手经验知道，维护甚至比第一次构建更难。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we believe product teams should focus engineering efforts and competitive advantages, not integrations.
zh: 我们相信产品团队应该集中精力在工程工作和竞争优势上，而不是集成上。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why companies like U.COM, AI21 and hundreds of others use Paragon to accelerate their integration strategy.
zh: 这就是为什么像 U.COM、AI21 和数百家其他公司使用 Paragon 来加速他们的集成战略。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you want to avoid wasting months of engineering on integrations that your customers need, check out Paragon at useparagon.com/lenny.
zh: 如果你想避免浪费几个月的工程时间在你客户需要的集成上，请访问 useparagon.com/lenny 查看 Paragon。

zh: 本期节目由 Pragmatic Institute 带给您，它是产品专业知识值得信赖的领导者。

en: Pragmatic Institute helps product professionals turn ideas into impact through proven courses, workshops and certifications designed for real-world success.
zh: Pragmatic Institute 帮助产品专业人士通过经过验证的课程、研讨会和认证将想法转化为影响力，这些课程专为现实世界的成功而设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: For over 30 years, they've trained more than 250,000 product leaders at companies like Google, Microsoft and Salesforce.
zh: 在过去的 30 多年里，他们培训了超过 25 万名产品领袖，来自像 Google、Microsoft 和 Salesforce 这样的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Equipping them with practical strategies to build and scale market-winning products.
zh: 为他们配备实用的策略来构建和扩展赢得市场的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pragmatic's full-time instructors each bring over 25 years of hands-on leadership experience, teaching strategies proven to deliver real-world results.
zh: Pragmatic 的全职讲师每个人都拥有超过 25 年的实际领导经验，教授经过验证的策略以提供现实世界的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's not just about what you learn, it's also about who you learn it with.
zh: 这不仅仅关乎你学到了什么，也关乎你和谁一起学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: Completing a course connects you to an active community of over 40,000 product professionals.
zh: 完成课程会让你连接到一个超过 4 万名产品专业人士的活跃社区。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll engage in meaningful conversations, collaborate with peers and mentors, and gain direct instructor access to refine your strategies and stay ahead of trends.
zh: 你将进行有意义的对话，与同行和导师合作，并获得直接的讲师指导来完善你的策略并保持领先趋势。

speaker: Unknown
en: Get 20% off with Code LENNY20 at pragmaticinstitute.com/lenny.
zh: 访问 pragmaticinstitute.com/lenny，使用代码 LENNY20 享受 20% 的折扣。

speaker: Unknown
en: Peter, thank you so much for being here and welcome to the podcast.
zh: Peter，非常感谢你的到来，欢迎来到播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm so thrilled to be here, really honored.
zh: 我很高兴来到这里，真的很荣幸。

speaker: Unknown
en: Looking forward to having a great time here.
zh: 期待在这里度过一段美好的时光。

speaker: Unknown
en: As we were preparing for this conversation, we were jamming on what we should focus on.
zh: 当我们为这次对话做准备时，我们在讨论应该关注什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's so much that we're going to talk about.
zh: 我们有很多要谈论的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: But something that you said was really interesting and I'm really excited to start with this, which is that, you've always felt that you haven't been able to say all the things you really think and feel because you've been within corporations, PR people keeping you on message, and this is the first time that you feel free to share.
zh: 但是你说的一些话真的很有趣，我真的很兴奋从这个开始，也就是，你一直觉得你没能说出你真正思考和感受的所有事情，因为你在公司内部，公关人员让你保持传达一致的信息，而这是你第一次感到自由分享。

speaker: Unknown
en: First time.
zh: 第一次。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so first of all, just how does that feel?
zh: 好的，那么首先，那感觉如何？

speaker: Unknown
en: Second of all, tell us something that you've been wanting to share or that you can finally talk about.
zh: 其次，告诉我们一些你想分享的内容或你终于能谈论的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, it feels really good.
zh: 嗯，感觉真的很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, let me ask... I love it that you're starting with a spicy question here and let me share some more context behind it.
zh: 那么，让我问……我很高兴你用一个尖锐的问题开始，让我分享一些更多背后的背景。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm here to speak more freely, but it's not really what you think.
zh: 我在这里是为了更自由地说话，但这并不是你想的那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not here to divulge any secrets from the companies.
zh: 我不是在这里透露公司的任何秘密。

speaker: Unknown
en: But naturally I'm kind of a storyteller, I'm kind of an introvert.
zh: 但天生我有点像个讲故事的人，我有点内向。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, this podcast, I feel like I have the ability to go deeper with you on any topic and kind of add the context.
zh: 所以，这个播客，我觉得我有能力与你深入探讨任何话题，并添加背景。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I think without some of the context, some of my spicy takes or whatnot might be taken out of context, and just not having the time pressure, not feeling like there's some PR message I have to hit, is just really freeing.
zh: 因为我认为如果没有一些背景，我的一些尖锐观点或其他什么可能会被断章取义，而且没有时间压力，不觉得有某些公关信息必须传达，真的让人很自由。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, it feels awesome, really anything that is on your mind that you should find interesting to your listeners, I'm here for it and yeah, I'm excited.
zh: 所以，感觉棒极了，只要是你脑子里认为对你的听众有趣的事情，我都在这里，是的，我很兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: Something I always tell guests, and I don't want people to take this out of context also, but I always describe myself as a reverse journalist where I want the guests to be the best version of themselves.
zh: 我总是告诉客人的一件事，我也不希望人们断章取义，但我总是把自己描述为一个反向记者，我希望客人展现他们最好的版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: I never want to catch people off guard or just say something they never meant to say.
zh: 我从来不想让人措手不及，或者说一些他们从未打算说的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: So-
zh: 所以-

speaker: Unknown
en: That's great.
zh: 那很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: ... it's a safe space.
zh: ……这是一个安全的空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But still, is there anything that you want to share or that might be interesting to share that you've been wanting to share that you haven't been able to?
zh: 但是，仍然有什么你想分享的或者可能有趣分享的内容，是你一直想分享却没能分享的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there anything along those lines?
zh: 有这方面的事情吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I always get this question around sort of, AGI, is it coming?
zh: 我的意思是，我总是会得到这类问题，大概是关于 AGI，它要来了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it going to solve everything?
zh: 它会解决一切吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: What have you seen?
zh: 你看到了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it's so interesting because when I was at OpenAI, it was around the time that people were really scared of AI and, "Oh, it's going to get rid of humans or it's going to do all these things."
zh: 我的意思是，这太有趣了，因为当我在 OpenAI 时，大约是人们真的害怕 AI 的时候，“哦，它要摆脱人类或者它要做所有这些事情。”

speaker: Unknown
en: But with every technology, I think everyone's been just kind of taking some time to acclimate to it.
zh: 但是对于每一种技术，我认为每个人都需要花一些时间来适应它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think with AGI it's a similar thing, which is it's so far out that everyone's like, "Well, what's our world going to be like?"
zh: 我认为对于 AGI 也是类似的情况，就是它还很遥远，每个人都像，“嗯，我们的世界会是什么样子？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And the real answer is none of us really know.
zh: 而真正的答案是我们谁都不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in terms of solving problems, I think some people believe AGI is going to solve everything, but I don't think so.
zh: 但在解决问题方面，我认为有些人相信 AGI 会解决一切，但我不这么认为。

speaker: Unknown
en: AGI is just necessary but not sufficient.
zh: AGI 只是必要条件但非充分条件。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of the value is still going to require a bunch of hustle from a lot of builders to really turn that new source of energy and channel it into something that we humans want to use that solves some of our problems.
zh: 很多价值仍然需要大量建设者的努力，才能真正将这种新能源引导成我们人类喜欢使用并解决我们某些问题的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that hustle is going to be required, that elbow grease is going to be required to really make AGI something useful.
zh: 这种努力将是需要的，这种苦干将真正使 AGI 成为有用的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your point is that people think AGI hits, all of a sudden all jobs are gone, AGI is doing everything.
zh: 你的观点是，人们认为 AGI 一出现，所有工作突然消失，AGI 正在做所有事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I think this is a optimistic message that things will be okay if AGI, basically AGI being, and I'm curious if you have a clear definition, but AGI being, AI being just basically as smart as humans-
zh: 因为我认为这是一个乐观的信息，如果 AGI，基本上 AGI 存在，我好奇你是否有清晰的定义，但 AGI 存在，AI 基本上和人类一样聪明——

speaker: Peter Deng
en: Look, I won't-
zh: 听着，我不会——

speaker: Unknown
en: ... generally.
zh: ... 一般来说。

speaker: Unknown
en: ... claim to be an expert on this at all, but I think that with every technology that's come out, we've been able to harness it and it takes a lot of harnessing.
zh: ... 声称我是这方面的专家，但我认为对于每一个推出的技术，我们都能够驾驭它，这需要大量的驾驭。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think I'm going to use that word very deliberately.
zh: 我想我会非常刻意地使用那个词。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll use something really basic.
zh: 我会用一个很基础的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: What seems obvious today is that, there was a time when databases were all the rage.
zh: 今天显而易见的是，曾经有一段时间，数据库非常流行。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, "Oh my goodness, you can store a bunch of data and you can query it really quickly and imagine all the possibilities."
zh: 这就像，“天哪，你可以存储一堆数据，你可以非常快地查询它，想象所有的可能性。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that a lot of amazing entrepreneurs and builders built some really great products on top of databases.
zh: 我认为许多伟大的企业家和建设者在数据库之上构建了一些非常棒的产品。

speaker: Lenny
en: That's right.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, that's kind of the basis of all the stuff that we're seeing today.
zh: 事实上，这就是我们今天看到的所有事情的基础。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it seems so obvious today, but I don't know, maybe in 10 years, 15 years when we look back, it's like, "Of course it made sense that we have this super intelligent thinking machine."
zh: 这在今天似乎显而易见，但我不知道，也许在 10 年、15 年后，当我们回顾时，这就像，“当然，拥有这个超级智能思维机器是有意义的。”

zh: 我认为人们想要做很多强行适配以适应某种原型。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm glad we talked about the PM archetypes.
zh: 我很高兴我们讨论了 PM 原型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hopefully that frees people up to really lean into what they love.
zh: 希望这能让人们真正自由地投入到他们热爱的事情中去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because life's pretty short.
zh: 因为生命相当短暂。

speaker: Unknown
en: It'd be great if everyone would find the thing that they really wanted to do, and be able to lean in and do that.
zh: 如果每个人都能找到他们真正想做的事情，并且能够投入其中去做，那就太好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the optimist to me is also why I'm so excited about the time and age that we're in right now, because there's so many different companies popping up.
zh: 我认为对我来说乐观主义者也是为什么我对我们所在的这个时代如此兴奋的原因，因为有这么多不同的公司涌现出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's something that really resonates with people.
zh: 所以有一些东西真正能与人产生共鸣。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, take a look at just what we're doing here, it's like, podcasting was not a thing 20 years ago.
zh: 我的意思是，看看我们在这里所做的，就像，播客在 20 年前还不是一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was not a thing.
zh: 它不是一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: But now, we are able to have these amazing tools and platforms that allow people to really express themselves, and really, what really truly brings them joy and makes them happy, and also brings a ton of value to the world.
zh: 但是现在，我们能够拥有这些令人惊叹的工具和平台，允许人们真正表达自己，真正地，真正真正给他们带来快乐和让他们幸福的事情，同时也给世界带来巨大的价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that, yeah, I definitely believe in leaning in strengths, and I think that as hard as it may be, sometimes you got to look at where you are right now, and is this the thing that you really want to do?
zh: 所以我认为，是的，我绝对相信发挥优势，我认为尽管这可能很难，有时你必须看看你现在在哪里，这是你真正想做的事情吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or is there something else that's drawing your attention and drawing you towards that?
zh: 或者还有其他什么在吸引你的注意力并把你拉向那个方向？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's another management oriented question I want to ask you.
zh: 我还有一个管理导向的问题想问你。

speaker: Unknown
en: This came from Eric Antonell, who apparently has worked with you for 17 years across a bunch of different-
zh: 这来自 Eric Antonell，他显然在许多不同的地方与你共事了 17 年

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, off and on for 17 years.
zh: 是的，断断续续地共事了 17 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of my biggest mentors and friends, he's amazing.
zh: 我最重要的导师和朋友之一，他很了不起。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he's like, "You need to ask this question."
zh: 所以他说，“你需要问这个问题。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So the way he put it is you've hired, managed, mentored many, many, many product people, some junior, some senior, across so many different cultures, and he's just like, "We need to learn something from your experience doing that," in terms of what you've learned about what it takes to be a really successful product person, whether it's being successful in building product or career-wise, what's just a nugget that you learned from seeing so many different types of people, and cultures, and seniority.
zh: 所以他提出的方式是，你聘用、管理、指导了很多很多产品人员，有些是初级，有些是高级，跨越了如此多的不同文化，他只是说，“我们需要从你的经验中学习一些东西”，关于你对成为真正成功的产品人员所需条件的了解，无论是构建产品成功还是职业发展方面，有什么你从看到这么多不同类型的人、文化和资历中学到的小贴士吗。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think for a product person specifically, it's really important to obsess over the details of craft.
zh: 我认为对于产品人员来说，沉迷于工艺的细节真的很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because ultimately, you're crafting a product.
zh: 因为归根结底，你在打造一个产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's important to obsess about the details of craft, while simultaneously having the perspective and wisdom of which details don't actually matter.
zh: 痴迷于工艺的细节很重要，同时也要拥有关于哪些细节实际上并不重要的视角和智慧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to pause there and just kind of try to-
zh: 我要在那里暂停，试着

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to pause there and just try to unpack this a little bit because at the core of being a product person, you're like, oh, I want to build something that people love and that's the job and that's what draws people to be product people is that you have this desire to build.
zh: 我要在那里暂停，只是试着稍微解释一下，因为作为产品人员的核心，你会想，哦，我想建立人们喜欢的东西，这就是工作，这就是吸引人们成为产品人员的原因，就是你拥有这种建造的愿望。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that I've been involved in enough teams where I, myself, and when I was really young and coming up as a product person, I would just get obsessed over these little details and I realized afterwards that we've just wasted a bunch of time on something that didn't actually matter.
zh: 我认为我参与过足够多的团队，我自己，当我还很年轻并成长为产品人员时，我会只是沉迷于这些小细节，而事后意识到我们只是在一些实际上并不重要的事情上浪费了一堆时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that dichotomy is somewhat interesting and beautiful to me because it capsulates both the core of what the ethos of a successful product person is, which is you really have to care and you have to give a crap about the product that you're building, but you also have to have the perspective and business know-how to understand where do you apply your time and where do you apply the care there?
zh: 所以我认为这种二分法对我来说有点有趣和美丽，因为它概括了成功产品人员精神核心的两个方面，就是你真的必须关心，并且要在乎你正在构建的产品，但你也要拥有视角和商业头脑来明白你在哪里应用你的时间，你在哪里应用你的关心？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I myself feel like I've gone through cycles.
zh: 而且我自己觉得我经历了周期。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything that I've done, I've gone super deep and really obsessed and then I take a step back and I'm like, wait, actually I was missing something and this other thing was more important, right?
zh: 我所做的每一件事，我都做得非常深入并且非常痴迷，然后我退后一步，我想，等等，实际上我错过了一些东西，而另一件事更重要，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll give you an example.
zh: 我给你举一个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll use the Uber example here as what I said that the digital product didn't really matter and it's all about the price, the ETA, one of the products that I've built at Uber, which is Uber Reserve, right?
zh: 我在这里用 Uber 的例子来说我之前所说的数字产品并不重要，一切都是关于价格、ETA，我在 Uber 构建的产品之一，Uber Reserve，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the simplest of things.
zh: 这是最简单的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Going back to what I said before, sometimes the best products is the simplest of things.
zh: 回到我之前说的，有时最好的产品是最简单的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the problem that we were trying to solve is that everyone has this.
zh: 但是我们要解决的问题是人人都遇到这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have a 6 AM flight, and are you really going to wake up at 4 AM and request an Uber and hope that there's enough Ubers and the person's going to come?
zh: 你有一个早上 6 点的航班，你真的要在早上 4 点醒来并请求 Uber 并希望有足够的 Uber 并且那个人会来吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because if you do that, you're not going to sleep well and you're going to wake up every two hours and you're probably going to miss your flight anyway because you're going to fall asleep or whatever.
zh: 因为如果你那样做，你不会睡得好，你会每两小时醒一次，你反正可能会错过你的航班，因为你会睡着或者别的什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there was this insight of like, okay, there's a whole mismatch between what people really want, which is the peace of mind that their car is going to be there and guess what?
zh: 所以有这样的洞察，好吧，人们真正想要的和实际之间存在完全的不匹配，也就是车会出现在那里的安心感，你猜怎么着？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm willing to pay for that.
zh: 我愿意为此付费。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we built Uber Reserve, which it was the simplest thing, which is like, oh, just go ahead and say what time your flight is and we'll work backwards or even just tell us when you want to get picked up and everything about that product we crafted what really mattered for the user, which was the peace of mind.
zh: 于是我们构建了 Uber Reserve，这是最简单的东西，就像，哦，直接说出你的航班时间，我们会倒推，或者甚至直接告诉我们你想被接走的时间，关于那个产品的所有内容，我们精心打造了对用户真正重要的东西，那就是安心。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you go there and you say what time your flight is and your pick-up time or whatever, I think that the product is... It hasn't changed that much since I was there.
zh: 所以如果你去那里，说出你的航班时间和接车时间之类的，我认为这个产品是……自从我在那里以来，它并没有太大的变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: It would tell you, oh, this is cutting it really close.
zh: 它会告诉你，哦，这太悬了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You may not make your flight.
zh: 你可能赶不上航班。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, wow.
zh: 就像，哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, that was put in there because of the principle of peace of mind.
zh: 同样，那被放在那里是因为安心的原则。

speaker: Unknown
en: And on the other side it's like, well, what do drivers need?
zh: 另一方面，就像，嗯，司机需要什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: They need to know you're not going to cancel and all this other stuff.
zh: 他们需要知道你不会取消，以及所有其他这些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you've got to think about the driver incentives too.
zh: 所以你也必须考虑司机激励。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was a simple idea, really proud of the team for figuring out all the intricate details, did some testing, and last I heard from folks internally, this is a $5 billion a year business now and one of the highest margin ones, and I'm really proud of this because it came from the idea of let's focus on what actually matters, which is that peace of mind and how many people really need it in that moment.
zh: 这是一个简单的想法，真的为团队弄清楚所有复杂的细节感到自豪，做了一些测试，据我从内部人员那里听到的最新消息，这是一项年入 50 亿美元的业务，也是利润率最高的业务之一，我真的为此感到自豪，因为它来自于让我们专注于真正重要的事情的想法，也就是那种安心，以及有多少人在那一刻真的需要它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that's the best story I can tell.
zh: 所以我认为这是我能告诉的最好的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's an awesome story.
zh: 这是一个很棒的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It connects so many of the things you've talked about.
zh: 它把你谈到的这么多事情联系在了一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is just it may not be the product that really matters, and micro-optimizing the experience is not going to move the needle when there's something else that's more operationally oriented, but there's always going to be a product component if you're building it for freezers.
zh: 一个是它可能不是真正重要的产品，当还有其他更偏向运营导向的东西时，微调体验是不会有太大作用的，但如果你是为冷冻柜构建产品，总是会有产品组件的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other piece that I think is interesting here is... Well, there's two.
zh: 我认为这里还有一点很有趣的是……嗯，有两点。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is just it connects back to your point about the importance of autonomy of product people is just I feel like you're like, here's the team, here's what I'm told to work on.
zh: 一个是它联系回你关于产品人员自主性的重要性的观点，只是我觉得就像你，这是团队，这是我被要求做的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you're like, oh, but this thing is actually the problem we need to solve and let's just build a new product around it.
zh: 然后你就像，哦，但这实际上才是我们需要解决的问题，让我们围绕它构建一个新产品吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there's a whole story I imagine of you getting buy-in and all that stuff.
zh: 然后我想象着有一个关于你获得支持以及所有那些事情的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other thing this connects to, we just had the CPO of Uber, the current CPO of Uber on the podcast, and he had a few episodes before this one.
zh: 这件事联系到的另一点是，我们刚请了 Uber 的 CPO，Uber 现任的 CPO 做客播客，他在这一期之前有几期。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was all about dog fooding and basically exactly discovering these problems.
zh: 全是关于亲身体验（dog fooding）以及基本上正好发现这些问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's done seven to 800 rides as an Uber driver to discover these problems.
zh: 他作为 Uber 司机做了 700 到 800 次行程来发现这些问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: He had this great quote about, it's one thing to watch, just build an app for drivers sitting in your office making it look really pretty.
zh: 他有一句很棒的引言关于，坐在办公室里为司机开发一个应用程序让它看起来非常漂亮是一回事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's another to be driving 60 miles an hour with this phone a few feet away from you trying to figure things out.
zh: 而以 60 英里的时速驾驶，这部手机离你只有几英尺远，试图搞清楚事情是另一回事。

speaker: Unknown
en: A hundred percent.
zh: 百分之百同意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, I remember that I took two weeks off before I joined Uber.
zh: 哦，我记得我在加入 Uber 之前休了两周假。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in that time I've been obsessed with user research for the longest of times, and this is more relevant back then when you wanted to really understand how the wide massive users were using your product.
zh: 在那段时间里，我一直沉迷于用户研究很久了，这在当时更相关，因为那时你想真正理解广泛的用户是如何使用你的产品的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember I actually leased a car to drive for Uber those two weeks.
zh: 我记得我实际上租了一辆车在那两周里为 Uber 开车。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was a little white VW something or another.
zh: 所以那是一辆白色的大众某种车之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I put an Uber sticker on it, I turned on the app and it just started driving and there's no better way to learn than to dog food, and I'll just build on what... Sachin is the person you had on the podcast?
zh: 我在上面贴了 Uber 贴纸，打开应用程序就开始开车，没有比亲身体验更好的学习方法了，我只想在 Sachin 说的基础上展开……Sachin 是你请到播客上的那个人吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, he's an amazing, amazing guy.
zh: 是的，他是个非常棒的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I'll just build on what he said there.
zh: 所以我只想在他所说的基础上展开。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that what really stuck with me in terms of framework that I learned back in school because I was brought up with the IDEO way of design thinking and I was at the design school at Stanford where before we literally were in trailers.
zh: 我认为对我来说真正让我印象深刻的是我在学校时学到的框架，因为我是在 IDEO 的设计思维方式中长大的，我在斯坦福的设计学院，那时我们真的在拖车里。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's how early it was.
zh: 那就是这么早的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I remember the framework that really stuck with me is what IDEO preached, which is there are five stages to great design thinking.
zh: 但我记得真正让我印象深刻的框架是 IDEO 所宣扬的，那就是伟大的设计思维有五个阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: Number one is empathize, two is to define, three is to ideate, four is a prototype, and five is to test.
zh: 第一个是同理心（empathize），第二个是定义，第三个是构思，第四个是原型，第五个是测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I love about this framework, and I really hope this doesn't get lost because I don't know how much it's being preached nowadays in design thinking is that it has the right words associated with it.
zh: 我喜欢这个框架的地方，我真的希望这一点不会丢失，因为我不知道如今在设计思维中宣扬了多少，就是它有与之相关的正确的词汇。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first thing is empathizing.
zh: 第一件事是同理心。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've got to really feel the pain of your customers.
zh: 你必须真正感受到客户的痛苦。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not just about theoretically understanding what the problems are.
zh: 这不仅仅是理论上理解问题是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really empathizing, which is why user research was so important to me is to understand that, or even like Sachin said, just taking those rides but also flying around the world.
zh: 这真的是同理心，这就是为什么用户研究对我来说如此重要，以理解这一点，或者就像 Sachin 说的那样，只是乘坐那些行程，但也飞往世界各地。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when I was working at Uber to figure out, well, what are the various conditions?
zh: 当我在 Uber 工作时，为了弄清楚，嗯，各种条件是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so empathize is a really powerful word.
zh: 所以同理心是一个非常强大的词。

speaker: Unknown
en: The define is also a really powerful word because it forces you to articulate what the problem is.
zh: 定义也是一个非常强大的词，因为它迫使你阐明问题是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is, again, going back to the language thing of you have to be very intentional about defining the problems that you want to solve and then ideate, we all know it's brainstorming and prototyping and tests are self-explanatory, but the first two stages I think are really insightful and it talks directly to what Sachin was saying.
zh: 同样，这又回到了语言的问题上，你必须非常有意识地定义你想要解决的问题，然后是构思，我们都知道这是头脑风暴，原型和测试是不言自明的，但我认为前两个阶段真的很有见地，它直接回应了 Sachin 所说的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've got to dog food because you really have to empathize and the great products are when you really feel the pain and you really empathize with what people are experiencing.
zh: 你必须亲身体验，因为你真的必须有同理心，伟大的产品是当你真正感受到痛苦并且你真的对人们的经历感同身受时。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a great connection to another podcast episode that came to mind as you were talking, the head of product at Linear, Nan, had this really great concept that's exactly what you're saying, which is as a product person, you want to feel the pain of your customer the same way they do.
zh: 这与你在说话时我想起的另一期播客节目有着很好的联系，Linear 的产品负责人 Nan 有一个非常棒的概念，完全符合你所说的，那就是作为一个产品人员，你想要像你的客户一样感受到他们的痛苦。

speaker: Unknown
en: You shouldn't stop asking questions to understand what they're telling you until you feel the pain that they feel and that'll help you.
zh: 在你感受到他们感受到的痛苦之前，你不应该停止提问去理解他们告诉你的事情，那将帮助你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Basically, that's like how to operationalize empathizing.
zh: 基本上，这就是如何将同理心操作化。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just do you feel the suffering?
zh: 就是你感觉到痛苦了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, and I really do hope product people still do this to this day because I think there's so many shortcuts that if people take, you're going to miss the point, right?
zh: 是的，我真的希望产品人员至今仍然这样做，因为我认为有很多捷径，如果人们走了捷径，你就会错过重点，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I still remember distinctly flying down to LA with Kevin Systrom to go do a user research study, and it was a one-way glass thing where we listened to people talk about Instagram and how they use Instagram, and there's no substitute for that.
zh: 我依然清晰地记得，和 Kevin Systrom 一起飞往洛杉矶去做用户调研，那是一个单面镜的房间，我们在那里听人们谈论 Instagram 以及他们如何使用 Instagram，那是无可替代的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that to anyone out there who's doing user interviews and then saying, hey ChatGPT, summarize the takeaways, you're missing the point.
zh: 我认为对于任何在做用户访谈然后说，嘿 ChatGPT，帮我总结要点的人来说，你们没抓到重点。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't empathize with the summary.
zh: 你无法对总结产生共情。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to be in the room fully immersed, no phones, just actually hearing the words and the intonation.
zh: 你必须人在房间里，全身心沉浸其中，没有手机，只是真正听到那些话语和语调。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's how you're going to get the full color.
zh: 那是你获得全貌的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: It makes me think Jeff Bezos has this great quote, if you have an anecdote and data and they're telling you different things, trust the anecdote.
zh: 这让我想起 Jeff Bezos 有一句名言，如果你有一个轶事和数据，它们告诉你不同的事情，相信轶事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, man.
zh: 噢，天哪。

speaker: Unknown
en: So many lessons.
zh: 太多教训了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so to start to kind of wrap up our conversation, we covered a lot of ground, I want to ask you about Facebook real quick.
zh: 好的，为了开始总结我们的对话，我们讨论了很多内容，我想快速问你关于 Facebook 的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you joined Facebook very early.
zh: 你很早就加入了 Facebook。

speaker: Unknown
en: Eric Antonow, who I've mentioned previously, told me that it was very strange that you left Google to join Facebook at that stage.
zh: 我之前提到过的 Eric Antonow 告诉我，你在那个阶段离开 Google 加入 Facebook 是很奇怪的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Google was killing it, on top of the world.

en: You had such a strong career path, things were going great, but you decided to take a big leap joining Facebook.

speaker: Unknown
en: What did you see?

en: Because I think there's something interesting here that we can learn about what you saw that may help other people decide where to go work.

en: I've always been enamored with this idea of understanding us as fundamentally human and how we're wired.
zh: 我一直很迷恋这个想法，即理解我们作为人类的本质以及我们是如何被构造的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember at the time talking to the folks at Facebook and seeing it, and this was back when people were like, oh, this is just a college site, and that was the vibe back then.
zh: 我记得当时和 Facebook 的人交谈并观察它，那时候人们还说，哦，这只是一个大学网站，那是当时的氛围。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what I saw was that the team and Mark and others really understood the fundamental human desires that people had to connect and feel lonely and to share, and they really got the right articulation of the problem they were trying to solve, which was to make the world more open and connected.
zh: 但我看到的是，团队和 Mark 以及其他人真正理解了人们想要连接、感到孤独以及分享的基本人类欲望，他们真正正确地表达了他们试图解决的问题，即让世界更加开放和连接。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this really resonated with me because again, I study a lot in college like psychology, and I was really enamored with this idea of how are we as humans fundamentally wired?
zh: 这真的引起了我的共鸣，因为我在大学里学习了很多心理学，并且我真的迷恋这个想法，即我们作为人类是如何被构造的？

speaker: Unknown
en: And it felt to me like a no-brainer to go work at Facebook because they saw how people were wired and how to actually build products that complement how people are wired.
zh: 对我来说，去 Facebook 工作似乎是不需要动脑筋的事，因为他们看到了人们是如何被构造的，以及如何实际构建与人类构造相辅相成的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it wasn't that they were trying to force fit something into something that was unnatural.
zh: 他们并不是试图将不适合的东西强塞进不自然的事物中。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was almost like how do we build technologies and products that actually augment our fundamental desire to stay connected?
zh: 这几乎就像是，我们要如何构建真正增强我们要保持连接这一基本欲望的技术和产品？

speaker: Unknown
en: And this goes back to why I think the power of wars is so important is because you take a look at some of the mission statements for Friendster or MySpace, I don't even know if they had mission statements or what they were, they were kind of vapid and they didn't really speak to the fundamental humanity of what Facebook was striving to build and that just deeply resonated with me.
zh: 这又回到了为什么我认为 wars 的力量是如此重要的原因，因为当你看看 Friendster 或 MySpace 的使命宣言，我不知道它们是否有使命宣言或者是什么，它们有点空洞，并没有真正说到 Facebook 试图构建的基本人性，那深深地引起了我的共鸣。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I remember spending time with Eric being like, "Hey, what should I do?
zh: 所以我记得花时间和 Eric 在一起，就像，“嘿，我该怎么做？

speaker: Unknown
en: Should I take this offer from Facebook or should I stay at Google?"
zh: 我应该接受 Facebook 的邀请还是留在 Google？”

speaker: Unknown
en: But ultimately it was just that deep resonance with my values of building things that were fundamentally human.
zh: 但归根结底，这与我构建根本上属于人类的事物的价值观有着深深的共鸣。

speaker: Unknown
en: And ultimately I think that for any startup out there, anyone building product, the more that you can get a good impedance match between what you're building and what humans fundamentally want and need, the more successful you're going to be.
zh: 归根结底，我认为对于那里的任何初创公司，任何构建产品的人来说，你在你构建的东西与人类基本需求和欲望之间获得的阻抗匹配越好，你就会越成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's my big answer.
zh: 所以这就是我的主要回答。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the secondary answer, I've always optimized for learning in my career, and this is a huge thing that I say to a lot of people because they look at sort of like, oh, you've been at all these companies, what's your secret?
zh: 我认为次要的回答是，我在职业生涯中一直以学习为优化目标，这是我对很多人说的一件大事，因为他们看着就像，哦，你去过所有这些公司，你的秘诀是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm like, well, I've just figured out that I want to go to the place where I can learn the most.
zh: 我会说，好吧，我只是弄清楚了我想去一个能学到最多东西的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for me, that wasn't really Google, but I had so much I wanted to learn from operating at Facebook.
zh: 对我来说，那不是 Google，但我有太多东西想从在 Facebook 的运营中学到。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at Facebook I would say, yeah, I was there for nine and a half years, but I always jumped around every two and a half or so when I feel like there was something new to learn.
zh: 而且在 Facebook 我会说，是的，我在那里待了九年半，但我总是每两年半左右跳一次槽，当我觉得有新东西要学的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's it.
zh: 就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I don't know if it's a secret or not, I got lucky and I was able to have opportunities to learn different things and different skills, and that served me quite well.
zh: 我的意思是，我不知道这是否是一个秘密，我很幸运，我有机会学习不同的东西和不同的技能，这对我很有好处。

speaker: Unknown
en: And regardless of any outcome, I would say that's just a great way to live your life personally is just to optimize for learning and those experiences and for me, moving to Facebook was that I saw so much learning that could have happened and it ultimately did happen.
zh: 无论结果如何，我认为这 personally 都是一种很好的生活方式，只是以学习为优化目标，为了那些经历，对我来说，转到 Facebook 是因为我在那里看到了如此多的学习可能发生，并且最终确实发生了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I feel like that was a good outcome too.
zh: 所以我觉得那也是一个很好的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: [inaudible 01:39:55] did it.

speaker: Unknown
en: So a couple takeaways here for folks that are maybe trying to decide between a couple roles, maybe deciding if they should leave and do something new is one, are you feeling like you're learning enough/is the new place you're thinking about going to help you learn a lot more?
zh: 所以为那些可能试图在几个角色之间做决定，也许在决定是否离开并尝试新事物的人们提供几个要点，第一，你觉得你学得够多了吗/你想去的新地方能帮你学到更多东西吗？

zh: 第二，他们构建的东西是否与人类行为一致？

zh: 所以当你谈到 Facebook 时，他们对人类行为有着这种真正独特的见解，这对你来说真的很重要，所以这是一个非常契合的选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: A hundred percent.

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the insight thing, thank you for summarizing that and drawing that out because it's also what I look for and what I want to partner with companies and startups now is do you have that unique insight?
zh: 我认为见解这个东西，谢谢你总结这一点并把它引出来，这也是我寻找的，也是我现在想与公司和初创公司合作的地方就是你有那种独特的见解吗？

speaker: Unknown

en: And that usually is a good indicator of a strong point of view, and having a strong point of view is really important because there's a saying that Mike and Kevin had at Instagram which is we may not be right, but at least we're not confused.
zh: 这通常是一个强有力的观点的良好指标，拥有一个强有力的观点真的很重要，因为 Instagram 有一句 Mike 和 Kevin 的话，我们可能不对，但至少我们不困惑。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's a beautiful phrase I thought because sometimes you've just got to go and do the thing that you think is right and the indecision is going to be one of the things that really gets you and bites you.
zh: 我认为这是一个美丽的短语，我认为因为有时候你只需要去做你认为正确的事情，犹豫不决真的会害死你并咬你一口。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that for me is something as I look for folks who have a strong conviction, whether it's the founders I support when I go join and be an operator at the company or the founders I support in my current role.
zh: 所以这对我来说是我在寻找有坚定信念的人时的一件事，无论是我加入公司成为运营者时支持的创始人，还是我在目前角色中支持的创始人。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow, I didn't know that.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我不记得那是我们谈论过的事情，但同样，这可能只是英雄所见略同，我们只是与 Mike 和 Kevin 以及 Tomer 这些不同优秀的人有相同的感觉。

zh: 我喜欢这次对话引用了多少集的内容。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: Most people go through a lot of failed initiatives, projects, career hits, so the question is just what's a product that you built and launched that was just a big failure?
zh: 大多数人都会经历很多失败的举措、项目、职业挫折，所以问题只是你构建和发布的哪个产品是一个巨大的失败？

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我会用你问问题的方式来问，这如何改变了你的思考和运作方式？

en: One example is, since we were talking about Instagram before, we tried to build a kind of camera first app at Instagram.
zh: 一个例子是，既然我们之前谈到了 Instagram，我们试图在 Instagram 构建一种相机优先的应用程序。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was called Bolt and it didn't work and the great levels of craft and design and the premise was essentially can we make it so it reduces the pressure to share, and you can open to a camera, you can just send some things to folks and you get some good feedback and you go from there.
zh: 它被称为 Bolt，它没有起作用，具有极高的工艺和设计水准，前提基本上是我们能否让它减少分享的压力，你可以打开相机，你只需要发送一些东西给人们，你会得到一些好的反馈，然后从那里开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was obviously the Instagram design team, so it was top-notch.
zh: 显然那是 Instagram 设计团队，所以是一流的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The app was designed really well.
zh: 这个应用程序设计得非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was really fast because it's the Instagram engineering team and they were just really good at making performant mobile apps.
zh: 它真的非常快，因为它是 Instagram 工程团队，他们真的非常擅长制作高性能的移动应用程序。

speaker: Unknown
en: It had all of the advantages that we had talked about that we valued at Instagram, but we launched it and I believe it was New Zealand or Australia and it didn't work.
zh: 它拥有我们谈论过的我们在 Instagram 看重的所有优势，但我们发布了它，我相信是在新西兰或澳大利亚，它没有起作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember the reason we knew this is as we were looking at sort of the retention graphs and retention is the key indicator in any product that you build, it's not the number of users, not the volume, it's actually retention and cohorted retention, you can [inaudible 01:44:00] the line and if it asymptotes, then you're in a good spot because that means that people over X period of time will continue to stay on the app and that just didn't happen.
zh: 我记得我们知道这一点的原因是我们正在查看留存图表，留存是你构建的任何产品中的关键指标，它不是用户数量，不是量，实际上是留存和同期群留存，你可以那条线，如果它渐近，那么你就处于一个有利位置，因为这意味着人们在 X 段时间内将继续留在应用程序上，但这并没有发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the learning here was that you can really have the best team in the world with the best product taste and you can't really predict what's going to hit on the first go.
zh: 我认为这里的经验教训是，你真的可以拥有世界上最好的团队，拥有最好的产品品味，但你无法真正预测第一次尝试就会成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: And failure is okay, you're just going to up and learn from that and nobody wallowed over that.
zh: 失败是可以的，你只会振作起来并从中学习，没有人对此感到沮丧。

speaker: Unknown
en: We actually had some technology that we built there that we were able to port over to the main app, which was really helpful, but to quote the great american poet Sean Carter, "It ain't a loss, it's a lesson."
zh: 我们实际上在那里构建了一些技术，我们能够将其移植到主应用程序，这真的很有帮助，但引用伟大的美国诗人 Sean Carter 的话，“这不是损失，这是教训。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's really important that you see that as a product person is that you don't see it as failure, you see it as kind of great.
zh: 我认为作为一个产品人，非常重要的一点是，你不要把它看作失败，你把它看作某种很棒的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now I'm that much smarter.
zh: 现在我聪明多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is something that I've just collected.
zh: 这是我刚刚收集到的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's other examples as well, but I think this is a good example of sort of something that's somewhat counterintuitive, that you have the best team, you're going to provide those hits over and over, but sometimes you can't predict those hits and you just have to have the wisdom to be like, okay, let's see what we can learn here, see what we can save here, and then move on.
zh: 还有其他例子，但我认为这是一个很好的例子，说明了一些有点反直觉的事情，你有最好的团队，你会一次又一次地提供那些成功，但有时你无法预测那些成功，你只需要有智慧，比如说，好吧，让我们看看我们能在这里学到什么，看看我们能在这里挽救什么，然后继续前进。

speaker: Unknown
en: I absolutely remember that product in launch or heard about it, but I also don't ever think about it.
zh: 我绝对记得那个产品和发布，或者听说过它，但我也不去想它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think it's a good reminder.
zh: 所以我认为这是一个很好的提醒。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because Instagram launching a new product that's trying to rethink the way you do your camera, that's a big deal.
zh: 因为 Instagram 发布一个新产品，试图重新思考你使用相机的方式，这是一件大事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I could see that being a really big deal for it not to work out.
zh: 所以我可以理解这对它来说是一件大事，却没有成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the same time, nobody remembers that really.
zh: 同时，没有人真的记得那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 没错。

en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

en: What are two or three books that you find yourself recommending most to other people?

en: This is easy for me.

en: Number one is Sapiens.

en: If you're a product person, you have to understand our own humanity if you want to build products for people, straight up.

speaker: Unknown
en: The second book I think for product folks is a classic one, which is The Design of Everyday Things by Don Norman.

speaker: Unknown
en: This may seem outdated and old, but I promise you it's not.

en: It really helps you understand physical product design, which is again, things that mold and shape to humanity.

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it gives you a good sense of that.
